procedures.name: Incident Registration

steps.text: Creation: To log any issue/interrupted service, create an Incident record(create_incident).
Mandatory Inputs: opened_by (user submitting), caller_id (user affected), short_description, impact, and urgency.
Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.
Default State: All new Incidents are set to state = new.

notes: Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.

procedures.name: Incident Lifecycle and Closure

steps.text: new → in_progress / on_hold / resolved
in_progress → on_hold / resolved
on_hold → in_progress (Must log on_hold_reason before transition)
resolved → closed / 'in_progress'
Resolution Requirement: An Incident cannot transition to resolved without mandatory fields: resolution_code, and resolution_notes (free-form text, max 2000 chars).
Closure Policy: The incidents that are in resolved states will transition to closed after 72 hours.

inputs.fact: current status and on_hold_reason of the incident

decisions.rule: on_hold → in_progress (Must log on_hold_reason before transition)
decisions.then: log on_hold_reason, then set status in_progress

must_not: An Incident cannot transition to resolved without mandatory fields: resolution_code, and resolution_notes (free-form text, max 2000 chars).
deadlines: The incidents that are in resolved states will transition to closed after 72 hours.

procedures.name: Change Management

steps.text: Creation: All changes must originate from a Change Request record.
Change Types (Enumeration): standard (pre-approved, low risk), normal (requires planning/approval), emergency (requires immediate CAB approval override).

Rollback Plan: No Change Request can move to state = scheduled without a documented rollback_plan and risk_assessment score (1-100).

procedures.name: Problem Management

steps.condition: a recurring incident pattern or a major incident is identified
steps.text: Trigger: A Problem must be created (create_problem) when a recurring incident pattern or a major incident is identified.
Linking: The Problem record must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.

Workaround: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.
Final State: A Problem transitions to closed only after the permanent fix has been successfully implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request.

procedures.name: Configuration Item (CI) Integrity

steps.text: Table: All IT assets must be recorded in the cmdb_ci table.
Relationship: You must enforce mandatory CI relationships. Use link_ci_relationship to establish the links.
CI State: Only CIs with state = in_use or state = maintenance can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in state = retired or state = disposed.
CI Owner: All CIs must have a recorded support_group and ci_owner ID.

procedures.name: Service Level Management (SLA)

steps.condition: status on_hold with one of the three reasons
steps.text: SLA Pause: The SLA timer must be paused (stage = paused) when the Incident is in state = on_hold and the on_hold_reason is one of the following enumerations: awaiting_customer_confirmation, awaiting_vendor_input, or awaiting_change_approval.
Breach: If the SLA exceeds its duration (stage = breached), the escalation flag on the Incident must be set to true, and an automatic notification sent to the Manager.

global_rules.rule: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.
You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.
Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.
Knowledge Scope: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.
User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.
Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.
You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.
When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.
The same is the case of optional or default arguments.
Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. Manages assignment rules, workflows, and ACLs.

Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ on access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations.

Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings.

Reporter (reporter) | IT Service Consumption | Can view and update their own submitted Incidents/Requests. Can search Public Knowledge articles. | Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes.
CI State: Only CIs with state = in_use or state = maintenance can be linked to active Incidents. Do not link CIs in state = retired or state = disposed.
User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.
Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied (e.g., Incident cannot close if related change_request is not closed).
Rate Limiting: If exceeded, pause and retry using Exponential Backoff.

escalation.name: Policy Violation
steps: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
must_not: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.

definitions.meaning: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation)

policy_questions.question: "First you must check the user information": which user is meant (the logged-in user, the caller, both), and what must happen when the role cannot be confirmed?
The Administrator row has no Critical Restrictions cell. Are there really no restrictions, including on approving a Change Request, which only the Manager row names?

The Manager grant names incident, problem, change, knowledge. Is the Manager forbidden on every other write tool: users, groups, locations, incident templates, CIs, services, SLA definitions, notifications, Incident SLA records?
The Agent grant does not name users, groups, locations, incident templates, SLA definitions, notifications or Incident SLA records. Is the Agent forbidden on the write tools of all of these?
Section 5 is titled "Configuration and Service Management (CMDB)". Does the Agent's CMDB grant include services and service offerings? The package assumes yes and does not forbid them.

Do the grants on incident, change and knowledge include the link tools (child incidents, knowledge links, change mappings, affected CIs)? The package assumes yes, although the Manager has only READ on CMDB and link_affected_ci_to_incident touches a CI.
The Reporter row says "view and update" but also "their own submitted". May a Reporter call create_incident? The package does not forbid it.
Which fields of their own incident may a Reporter update? The Agent row names assignment, state and resolution; the Reporter row names none.

May a Reporter read records other than their own incidents and Public Knowledge (users, groups, services, changes, problems, SLAs)? The row grants nothing else but forbids only other users' records, CMDB and internal work notes. The package forbids only CI read tools.
Which field decides that a record is the Reporter's own, opened_by or caller_id? create_incident has no opened_by, and caller_id is the user affected, who may be another person.
Does "CMDB" in the Reporter restriction also cover list_incident_affected_cis and service or service offering reads? The deny rule covers only configuration item tools.

Approval Gate (4.1:4) requires a sys_approval record with status = approved for the move authorize to scheduled, but no tool reads or writes sys_approval. Who gives the approval, and may an Agent make the move or only a Manager? Which other approvals are mandatory (preamble:4)?
Which tools change "system administration settings", which the Agent cannot do?

"Requests", "Service Requests" and "Tasks" have no tool in the tool list. Does the policy mean incidents here, or do these parts have no effect? The same question holds for the service_catalog_item in 5.2:2.
The Manager "Can reassign incidents/requests" and the Agent "Can update assignment". Is reassigning an incident that already has an assignee open to both roles?

Priority "is determined automatically by the system" from a matrix that this text does not give (see the next question), and create_incident stores the default planning when priority is omitted. Must the agent pass a priority, or leave it out?
If a request states a priority, must the agent halt under Policy Violation, or create the record with the priority of the system? May any role override it?
When impact or urgency changes on update_incident, must priority be set again? The rules check only the create tools.
create_change requires priority and impact, but the policy has no matrix for changes and the change has no urgency, and rule 1:9 says never to assume. How must the agent get the priority of a change?
SLAs are aligned based on priority, but applies_to_priority of an SLA definition does not accept planning. Does an incident of priority planning have no SLA?
"halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing": what does pausing mean for the agent, ending the task, or waiting for the next user message?
Which endpoints are the "approved batch endpoints"? Is add_child_incidents one of them?
"return the list": which list is meant when a request is ambiguous, the records that match?

A mandatory field that is an identifier (caller_id) is missing: 1:4 says state which field is required, 1:7 says perform lookups. Which holds when a name is given but no ID, and which when nothing is given?
"all mandatory fields": only section 3 names mandatory fields. Which are mandatory for the other records and for update calls: the tool's required list?
"The same is the case of optional or default arguments": may the agent pass an optional argument the request does not state, for example a tool default such as category?
opened_by is a mandatory input, but create_incident has no such argument. Where does the agent record it, or is it dropped? The rule requires the other four inputs only.
A call gives assigned_to but no assignment_group. Is the group of the incident the "specified" one, or is the membership not checked?
"on_hold → in_progress (Must log on_hold_reason before transition)": is the reason logged when the incident enters on_hold, or before it leaves on_hold?
Does the system close resolved incidents after 72 hours, or must the agent? May an agent close one before 72 hours pass, as the transition resolved → closed allows?
The tools accept status canceled for an incident; the policy lists five states without it. Is canceled forbidden? The transition rule has no edge to it.

Section 9 lists resolution_code values fixed, workaround, not_reproducible, closed_by_caller; the tools accept only Duplicate, Known Error, No resolution provided, Resolved By Caller, Resolved By Problem, Resolved By Change, Solution Provided, Workaround Provided, User error. Which list holds, and is there a mapping?
Change type (standard, normal, emergency) has no argument in create_change or update_change, only category and cab_required. Where is the type recorded? Must cab_required follow from it?
What counts as a "recurring incident pattern" (how many incidents, in what time) and as a "major incident" (priority critical)?
There is no incident_to_problem related list in the tools. Is the link made by the problem argument of update_incident?
There is no workaround_notes field. Into which field of a linked incident (worknotes, description) and of a knowledge article is it published, and which articles are "relevant"?
May a Problem that is already past fix_in_progress get a corrected workaround without going back to fix_in_progress?
What proves that the permanent fix was "successfully implemented": a mapped change with status closed and close_code successful, or status implement or review?
Status in_stock is in neither sentence of the CI State rule. Is it forbidden, as "Only" says? The rule forbids it.
Which incident statuses are "active Incidents"? May an in_stock or retired CI be linked to a resolved or closed incident? The rule does not look at the incident.

"Metrics tracked are limited to response_time and resolution_time": the tools have metric with values response and resolution, and target_mins. Are response_time and resolution_time the metric values response and resolution? Does this forbid any argument of an SLA definition?

Who pauses the SLA timer, the system or the agent? If the agent, the Agent, Manager and Reporter grants name no SLA record, so the grant rules and the duty conflict for update_incident_sla_details. Nothing decides, so both stay at remind.
The SLA Pause text says the Incident is in "state = on_hold", but incident has status, not state. Is status meant? The rule assumes yes.
The escalation flag on the Incident has no argument in update_incident. How is it set?
"an automatic notification sent to the Manager": does the system send it, or must the agent call send_notification? Which Manager (the manager_id of the group, any user with role manager)?
"Public Knowledge" and "published": does Public also mean visibility = external? May a Reporter find a published internal article?
How is a knowledge article "relevant" or "matching" (which search field, how close)?

When a Reporter creates an incident, 7:2 requires a knowledge link, but the Reporter grant does not name link_knowledge_to_incident, and the Reporter finds only published articles. Is the link still made, and by whom? Nothing decides, so both stay at remind.
"any user being ... updated is users.active = true": does this forbid update_user_details on an inactive user, including setting active back to true?

Which are the "mandatory dependencies" to verify before closing a record? The text gives one example (an Incident cannot close if its related change_request is not closed) and 4.2:5 names one for a Problem. Which other dependencies and records are meant, and which change statuses count as closed?

"All work logs (work_notes and activity_log)" must include sys_created_on and user_id, but worknotes is one text argument of the incident and problem tools, activity_log has no tool, and sys_created_on is not an argument. Must the agent write the timestamp and user_id into worknotes?

The Administrator row now also says the Administrator "Manages assignment rules, workflows, and ACLs". No tool changes assignment rules, workflows or ACLs. Does the sentence limit or grant anything the package must enforce?

The Agent row no longer says "READ access to all the tables". May the Agent read tables that are outside its Full CRUD list (users, groups, locations, services, SLA definitions, notifications)? The package forbids the Agent only some write tools.
Priority Calculation points to "a pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency", but this text has no matrix. Which matrix applies? The package derives no priority.

Which rules does the "Assignment Rules Engine" hold, and how does the agent follow them? No tool reads them. Must the agent set assigned_to and assignment_group from the engine, or leave the choice to the engine?

Where are rollback_plan and a risk_assessment score (1-100) recorded? update_change has implementation_plan, testing_plan and risk (high, medium, low), and no score. Does implementation_plan mean the rollback plan?

"Use link_ci_relationship to establish the links": there is no such tool. Which CI relationships are mandatory, and how does the agent link CIs (link_affected_ci_to_incident links a CI to an incident only)?

CI Owner now needs a recorded support_group and ci_owner ID. register_configuration_item has owner_id but no support_group or ci_owner. Is ci_owner the owner_id, and where is the support_group recorded? The rule requires owner_id only, at remind.

The policy lists the on_hold_reason values awaiting_customer_confirmation, awaiting_vendor_input, awaiting_change_approval and other. The tools accept only Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller and Awaiting Problem. Which list holds, and is there a mapping? The enumeration rule and the SLA pause duty stay at observe.

Who prompts the Agent to create the knowledge draft, and when: at the call that sets the status resolved, or before the move to closed (final closure)? What is a "simple password reset"? 7:3 names the Agent, but the duty would also apply when a Reporter resolves an incident, and the Reporter grant forbids create_knowledge_article. Nothing decides, so both stay at remind.

Use Tracking lists the types suggested, applied (used for resolution) and workaround, with the name kb_use. The tool link_knowledge_to_incident accepts suggested, applied and resolution in used_as. Which list holds? The rule on the values stays at observe.

The policy now writes state for incidents (3.1:5, 3.3:2, 6:3, 9:5), change requests (4.1:4, 9:9) and configuration items (5.1:4, 9:10), and workflow_state for knowledge articles (7:1, 9:11). The tools have status arguments for incidents, changes and configuration items, and state for knowledge articles. Does state mean the status argument? The rules use the names of the tools.
